answer: New identities enter only through an inlet of endorsements: three established peers must stake reputation on the newcomer, and each endorsement is a public edge that decays if the newcomer misbehaves. A farm cannot mint trust in bulk — like water crossing a dune field, every fake must walk a separate, costly path through real relationships, and one bad opal in the chain burns the sponsors' standing too. Honest agents pay nothing but their history.
